title: Idol John Marrero and banjo influences
summary: He names John Marrero and others he copied, remembers local halls, Sam Morgan, and avoiding the WPA.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: When you were coming up, you know like when you first started playing banjo, your idol was John Marrero. That's right.

One of them, I always met John Marrero, but John Sincero was living up in Chicago, I think, and I used to copy some of his stuff. And I actually copied some of Les Paul, the other guy who used to be with, Benny Goodman, a black fellow, he died. He's all a Christian. He's a great way. You have to do that to keep yourself voices down, you see.
What did you like about Marrero? I mean you took over, I mean you saw him quite a bit, I gather, down here. What about his playing did you like? I've never saw him.

Well the whole band itself, my daddy was very rich and my daddy were very good friends, and also some other things. I don't know what's happening. John, no, that's how this happened. Well I used to listen to that fellow, young fellow, you'd go to dances and things like that, and listen to that, the fellow's playing. And they had another fellow named Cap of Daringberg who played on the roof garden after John Grabber and we, I still call it, I don't know what they call it, something else, the building is still there. And they had the Pelican Hall, they had a lot of places down in this area, they had a hall, and I used to go down and listen to that Sam Morgan band, see. They were very seldom used as piano. And you admired a fellow that was older than you and played better than you. And another fellow when we had the, when we had the, when we had the Depression, when we had the, I don't know what they called it, in other words, he used to go to rehearsal every day, and you got paid, you know, and I was still in the Depression. With WPA? WPA. Yeah. I didn't join that because I was with this first wife of mine, I was standing on the Harbour and something, and the supper I was working with the city band, and I used to arrange the fellows, and I'd have different little groups and bands and things, and it was in my way. In fact I did better than playing music and writing arrangements and teaching than if I'd went on the WPA because I'd have been confined to go to rehearsal every day, see. So I made that out there. And this Nelson, he was with Sidney Duesley Band at the time, and the guys that were living with, most of the guys were probably dead now, yeah. But I would never thought about playing band, you know. And that E-Haw program, I would have listened to that one in which bar radio, one out from, was that Tennessee, the old opera house, and the E-Haw program. I'd have listened to all that kind of stuff, way back there, my radio, see.
